practice_standard._doc: Declared source classes for the practice pipeline (Item 320 Part 9, 29 Oct 2026). Read by practice.py before any read and by the standard generation; one definition.

two_windows.Window test: measures our reading: the most recent date of ours on the row must fall inside the window (Item 320 Part 1 ruling)
two_windows.practice window: measures the signal’s currency: the signal’s publication date must fall inside the window (Item 320 Part 8 ruling); the read date on the line dates our check

sunbiz.what: Florida Division of Corporations — reads only, never writes; stays at 0 reads absent a Chair ruling revisiting the Part 6 ceiling and the 0-Sunbiz posture

job_board.what: job boards, for the Fractionals criterion

practice_standard.company_site: not a source for any criterion
practice_standard.no_signal_found_rule: derived only when every declared source class permitted for the criterion was read for the row and nothing returned; the classes read are logged on the row

read_cost.measured: Part 7 measured a median 0.47 s per read on 135 reads; cost in reads per row per class is measured in this part and stated in bot-report-part9.json

Acquisitions.what: sale posture, succession or ownership transition
Acquisitions.source_rule: third parties only (brokers, trade press, registries); never the company's own site

Fractionals.what: a published finance or operations vacancy, an interim-leadership announcement, or a first-finance-hire posting
Fractionals.source_rule: a published posting or announcement, with its source and date

Private Equity.what: a Florida sponsor's published portfolio, platform or add-on announcement
Private Equity.source_rule: the sponsor's or the press's publication, with its source and date

practice_standard.rule: derived from dated signal lines and read-no-signal lines on the row; never typed; the bot's Part 7 sentences enter as not read until a human reads them; a signal dated outside the window reads no signal found

measured: 2026-10-29 (classifier pass: trading check dated on its own line; source_state from the Src line; Band 2 second entry; no sourced row labelled unsourced)
note: Re-run audit.py after any upload of florida.html; the console reads this file as Phase 3’s table.

florida100_close.ruling: the Chair: the Florida 100 closes at its measured count — a route tested and found absent, not a shortfall

measured.feed_full_pass_rate: about 1–2 companies reaching tests 1, 2 and 5 per window at 70–135 reads; 0 in window sixteen; the Private Equity and Fractionals feed queues exhausted
measured.sponsor_roster_hig: 377 entries read in full; 28 Florida by the Location field (~7%); 6 passing test 1 (~1.6%); about one read per entry, because location is not on the listing’s face
measured.association_rosters: FRLA, the Manufacturers Association of Florida, the Florida Trucking Association: no member directory linked from the home page; FloridaMakes: directory linked, 404 — none readable (scope: these four)
measured.revenue: no free route produced a published revenue figure for any of the companies passing every other test; two figures found were above the ceiling (SeaWorld $1.66B, Mainline over $1B); size ruled Blind at window fifteen
measured.completion: every admission after window fifteen came from completing rows already found (a named executive), not from discovery

for_the_next_market: completion beats discovery: start from the rows already on file
a roster pays only where location is on the listing’s face
revenue for private companies at this size is not published on free routes; decide the size rule before the run, not after
prove every instrument on both sets — what it must stop and what it must keep — and gate the run on the proofs
count every check from its own counter; a zero must say whether it ran
florida100_close.faults: 1–61, in founders-roster.json and the window reports

findings_for_the_next_market: the press feed admits about one row per ~100 reads; sponsor rosters about one per ~280; every other class admitted none
marketplaces anonymise listings by design: a for-sale signal never names its company — closed, not re-tried
rosters pay in reads only where the listing carries the city on its face; of 45 roster-class sources probed in Florida, none did
registry, vacancy, association and fraud sources answered (or refused) without a company list on their face; Sunbiz and the WARN list refuse this reader
completion costs about 5 reads per finished row against ~100–280 to discover one: start a market from the rows on file
decide the size rule before the run: private revenue at this size is not published on free routes

call_ready.named decision maker: a person with a title on the row, from a dated source
call_ready.contact: a published phone or email on the row with a dated read on the row (Src: or Address source); a role inbox is flagged and counts as contact, distinct from a named individual
call_ready.practice fit: the row passed the market standard’s tier test (A, B, or Unverified intake); Tier C failed it
call_ready.signal: a dated third-party practice signal where one exists; Blind recorded where it does not — it does not block a dial

dial_rules.call_ready: a named decision maker with title from a dated source; a published phone or email with a dated read (role inbox flagged); practice fit by the market standard’s tier test
dial_rules.verified_callable: call-ready, and trading confirmed on the company’s own pages with an address sourced inside the window (the Core BD Report’s test)
dial_rules.blind: a Blind signal does not block a dial
dial_rules.classifiers: a classifier’s output is read before it is written or counted
dial_rules.closures: a closure is keyed on the host it measures
dial_rules.officers: an officer binds to a company by one clause’s grammar, never by span
dial_rules.portfolio_band: a Private Equity row is not capped at $25M: the counterparty is the sponsor; the qualifier is the sponsor relationship and the operating problem. The $25M band governs Fractionals and Acquisitions, where the owner is the buyer (ruled 2026-10-31)
dial_rules.route: Florida is a phone market: 2 named addresses against 31 role inboxes across 98 call-ready rows; email follows a connected call (measured 2026-10-31)
dial_rules.two_addresses: a register address and a row city that differ are both recorded, each labelled by what it is; neither overwrites the other (ruled 2026-10-31)
dial_rules.rows_or_companies: every count states whether it is rows or companies (all 27 markets)
dial_rules.self_overlap: the self-overlap check is owed in every market before its figures are stated; until it runs, that market’s company counts are unknown, not merely unverified
dial_rules.tier_contest: a tier contested across two files is resolved by evidence: Tier C governs only where the Tier C row names its screen-out; unevidenced Tier C yields; two named reasons that disagree are held

florida_close.dialable_universe_measured: florida.html Tier A 47 + Tier B 45, expansion main A 12 + B 4, intake 7
florida_close.call_ready: 98 rows across 97 companies (93 + 2 + 3 + 1 − 1 Correct Craft, resolved to Tier C by evidence)
florida_close.completion_cost: run three: 87 reads, 13 completions, 6.7 reads each
florida_close.call_ready_lineage: 93 + 2 (register) + 3 (queue) + 1 (Martinez expansion row) = 99 call-ready rows across 98 distinct companies
